key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Acute, often after EMOTIONAL or PHYSICAL STRESS. LOCATION: Chest (retrosternal). RADIATES to arm, jaw. DURATION: Minutes to hours. CHARACTER: Chest pain, pressure, dyspnea mimicking myocardial infarction (MI). AGGRAVATING: Recent severe emotional stress (death of loved one, bad news, argument). RELIEVING: Supportive care. TIMING: Acute onset after stressor. SEVERITY: 7-9/10. KEY POSITIVES: Postmenopausal woman, recent severe stress or emotional event, electrocardiogram (ECG) mimics myocardial infarction (MI) (ST elevation or T-wave inversion), normal coronaries on angiography, apical ballooning on echo. KEY NEGATIVES: NO significant coronary artery disease (differentiates from true myocardial infarction ).

red_flags: Severe chest pain mimicking myocardial infarction (MI)
